text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPEN — Dedicated EU pool saturation — p99 latency breach (streaming stalls)
incident-bot: Severity: P1 · Affected: dedicated-eu-pool-12 · Symptoms: p95 ~ 800ms -> p95 ~ 2.5s, p99 > 6s, streaming stalls observed, error rate small but backpressure increasing
incident-bot: Pager: ryan_oncall · Runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-warmup-autoscale.md
ryan_oncall: On it. Initial checks: is this localized to pool-12 only?
maria_prod: I'm seeing the same signal from EU region dashboards — queue depth jumped rapidly ~08:02 UTC, warmup success rate dropped to ~40% for recent handshake attempts
anu_sre: Adding some telemetry: autoscaler logs show repeated failed handshake timeouts around 08:01-08:06, then a flood of queued requests. Possible cold warmup storm.
lee_runtime: Confirmed. Kernel selection metrics show many instances starting with quantized kernel fallbacks which take longer to init. This delays acceptance of streaming sessions.
jordan_support: Any customer-visible errors? Support thread shows a handful of customers reporting streaming stalls and partial responses, notably customer-hr-prod and analytics-inc. They flagged token drops during streaming.
ryan_oncall: Copy. Priorities: 1) reduce customer impact, 2) triage root cause. Quick mitigation ideas: temporarily divert new sessions to hosted fallback, throttle low-priority queues, or do manual pool scale. Thoughts?
maria_prod: Hosted fallback is possible but might cost us. Throttling non-SLA traffic helps. We should also check warmup agent health — maybe some warmup tasks are getting OOM or stuck.
anu_sre: Pulling warmup agent logs now. Relevant tail:```
2026-03-15T08:01:03Z warmup-agent[pool-12] INFO starting warmup for slot-7
2026-03-15T08:01:04Z warmup-agent[slot-7] WARN kernel-load-time=12000ms
2026-03-15T08:01:05Z warmup-agent[slot-7] ERROR handshake-timeout
2026-03-15T08:02:10Z autoscaler INFO requested-scale +6 slots
2026-03-15T08:02:11Z autoscaler WARN handshake-latency-increase
```
anu_sre: Looks like kernel-load times spiking to 10-15s which cascades into handshake timeouts.
lee_runtime: That aligns with a recent kernel kernel-cache eviction that happened after low-memory compaction yesterday. Investigating kernel artifact cache.
ryan_oncall: Can we hot-warm slots (preload KV + short prefix) instead of full warmup to reduce time? Any risk?
maria_prod: We have a hotshot path we can trigger for priority customers — it preloads minimal KV and accepts streaming but with limited prefix cache. We'll need a config flip.
jordan_support: If we flip that, we should notify customers in the two affected support threads and add an incident banner.
anu_sre: Manual scale: I can request extra reserved slots from Dedicated pool (if capacity available). That helps short-term but if kernel load remains slow, new slots will also struggle.
lee_runtime: Short-term mitigation we can do immediately: 1) enable hotshot warmup mode for pool-12 (reduced kernel set), 2) throttle non-SLA class-3 requests at edge (drop or queue behind), 3) start manual autoscaler override + pre-pull cache artifacts to instances. I'll prepare commands.
ryan_oncall: Do it. Execute in order and post commands/logs here. Keep me looped for handoff.
lee_runtime: Running hotshot flip:```sh
# flip hotshot flag for pool-12
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/svc/pool-config/pool-12/flip -d '{"hotshot":true}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN"
```
lee_runtime: Flag set. Warmup logs now showing faster path:```
2026-03-15T08:08:22Z warmup-agent[slot-10] INFO hotshot-warmup start kernel-load-time=900ms
2026-03-15T08:08:23Z warmup-agent[slot-10] INFO handshake-success
```
maria_prod: Edge throttle rule applied to class-3 traffic: rule-id throttle-2026-03-15-01. Non-SLA queue depth reduced by ~60% within 30s. Metrics: queue_depth pool-12 -> 1200 -> 480.
jordan_support: Posted customer banner and notified top affected customers. Support has prioritized remediation tickets for customer-hr-prod and analytics-inc.
anu_sre: Manual scale request issued (+8 slots). Autoscaler gave capacity, but new instances will come up with hotshot path now — should be quicker.
ryan_oncall: Good. Monitoring p95/p99 and streaming error rate. Update every 2 mins.
lee_runtime: Pushing pre-pull artifact to kernel cache for remaining slots now:```sh
# artifact pre-pull
for i in $(seq 1 8); do ssh slot-$i "curl -s https://artifact-cache/kernels/latest -o /var/cache/kernel && sync"; done
```
maria_prod: Quick numbers: p95 dropped to 1.1s, p99 dropped to 2.3s, streaming stalls reports down ~80% in last 4m. Queue depth steadying.
anu_sre: Still seeing intermittent tail spikes on some long-context sessions — looks like KV cache misses on specific model variants. Investigating reroute to variant with smaller kv overhead.
ryan_oncall: If tail spikes persist beyond 15m, plan B is to route new long-context requests to a different region (eu-west-2 -> eu-west-1) or enable degraded streaming mode (lower chunk sizes). Which is faster?
lee_runtime: Region reroute requires routing table update and some customers have affinity enforced. Degraded streaming mode is faster and reversible. Recommend degraded streaming mode if tail persists.
maria_prod: Agree. We'll prep degraded streaming toggle and customer comms.
jordan_support: Support ready to update customers if we flip degraded streaming.
anu_sre: Telemetry 08:18: p95=850ms, p99=1.9s, streaming-error-rate ~0.2% (was 1.4%). Queue depth 360. Warmup success rate >90 on hotshot path.
ryan_oncall: Nice work. Keep autoscaler overrides for another 30m and prepare a postmortem checklist. I'll hand off to follow-up shift in 25m.
lee_runtime: Noted. I'll leave hotshot flag on and set an automatic revert in 35m unless we see regressions. Also will open a bug for kernel-cache eviction flow.
maria_prod: I'll draft incident summary for customers and a short SLO impact note (p99 breach window ~08:01-08:10 UTC).
jordan_support: Customer notice drafted and queued for send after review.
anu_sre: Quick root cause suspicion: compaction/eviction job ran and removed kernel artifacts which made warmup fall back to heavy kernel loads — triggers handshake timeouts under burst. We'll correlate with infra compaction job logs.
ryan_oncall: Thanks all. I'll close the page when metrics stable for 20m. If anyone sees regression ping here.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — p99 improved, currently monitoring.
